prompt:
The safety walk on this plant falls due on Friday, so the marking gang lays the three shots of one run onto a single sheet for the file before the inspector arrives.

The run starts at a pump whose nameplate is stamped CONDENSATE RETURN and ends at a dryer in the finishing shop. Between them the pipe is banded in three places: at the pump, at the wall penetration, and at the shop end. A code sheet clipped to the page gives the works marking rule. Every band carries a ground colour, a narrower ring of a second colour, an arrow, and the name of the fluid in letters; the rule sets a green ground with a black ring against condensate return, a green ground with a blue ring against cooling water, and a plain blue ground against compressed air. All three shots are lit cold white.

What each band takes, and which way each arrow heads, is what the file does not say.
easy_question: Is this one page made up of three photographs of the same pipe banded at different places along its run? Answer yes or no only.

steps.ask: Look at the letters on each of the three bands along this run. Answer with one of: all three bands carry the same fluid name; the bands carry a mixture of fluid names; the band at the pump is the only one carrying a fluid name.

Look at the arrow painted on each of the three bands along this run. Answer with one of: every arrow heads away from the pump end; every arrow heads back to the pump end; the arrows head different ways along the run.
